I have mixed feelings about this game.

It has really good voice acting, a top-tier soundtrack, and a charming art style. However, the turn-based mechanics aren't great. I don't even think it qualifies as a true turn-based game. It feels like playing Dark Souls, but with turn-based combat. The core gameplay lacks depth. All you need to do is build Maelle (since she deals 99% of your party's damage) and fill the other two slots with anyone. You just have to memorize enemy attack patterns to dodge or parry, you know, just like in Dark Souls. It also lacks build variety. The game just forces you to stack as much DPS as possible.

It’s a good game, but I don't think it’s the "best turn-based game" everyone claims it is. It doesn't even compare to BG3.

I'm writing this at not even two hours in, and hey, if things change, I'll update my review. But as of right now, this game already feels like a GOTY contender to me.

First, the opening might feel a bit slow, but it is building things up in the best possible way. Once this game hits, it HITS. It is gorgeous, the music is beautiful, and the writing has actually be surprisingly good! What's more, the way they are willing to have the characters NOT speak at times, and just subtly emote and live in a moment is worthy of praise. Too many games have characters self-narrate every little thing, and I really appreciate that this game doesn't feel that need (at least not nearly as strongly).

Also, I'm not typically a huge fan of jrpg-style turn-based combat, but it feels good here! It's fast and stylish (reminiscent of Persona 5), and the active dodge/parry is just enough to keep me fully engaged.

I'm sure this game won't be for everyone. After all, some people don't like good things.

This game will remind you why you fell in love with gaming. It will also teach you that your struggle with gaming doesn't necessarily stem from the fact that you're getting older and have less time, but rather, games have lost a lot of their former experimental, risk-taking, creative spark, which has slowly eaten away at how fun they are to play. This game is so good the grind doesn't feel like a grind, and exploring the map doesn't feel like checking off a list of to-dos. It feels like... well, fighting, growing, and exploring. When you have finished this game (and probably tackled most if not all of the optional content), it will leave a void - because you know there will not be another like it for a long time.

The story demands your attention. The voice acting is excellent along with interesting places to explore so far. (Just 5 hours in). This is well done and I believe has the secret sauce to make this game stand out from the rest as proven through out the year with awards and gross sales. Great work and thank you.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the most impressive RPGs I have ever played. From the very beginning, the game captivates players with its unique world, emotional storytelling, and stunning visual design. The art style is absolutely beautiful, blending fantasy and surreal elements to create environments that are both mysterious and unforgettable.

The story is the heart of the experience. It delivers powerful emotional moments, memorable characters, and a narrative that keeps you invested from start to finish. Every member of Expedition 33 feels important, with their own personalities, motivations, and character development that make the journey meaningful.

Gameplay is equally outstanding. The turn-based combat system feels fresh and engaging thanks to its interactive mechanics, rewarding both strategy and timing. Battles remain exciting throughout the adventure, while character progression offers plenty of customization options.

The soundtrack deserves special praise as well. Its emotional and atmospheric music perfectly complements the game's dramatic moments and breathtaking locations.

Overall, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is a masterpiece that combines exceptional storytelling, fantastic gameplay, gorgeous visuals, and an unforgettable soundtrack. It is a must-play RPG and easily earns a 10/10 rating from me.

I’m a 40 year old (ish) dad with toddlers running around, and have found this is a great respite when I can find some downtime. Combat is challenging, story is compelling enough to stick with it, and the setting is beautiful. Love the fantasy with a European twist. Highly recommend this expertly crafted experience. Will definitely be on the lookout for the next delivery from this studio.

Enemy variety throughout each level is very lacking. Often you will fight the same 2 enemies 10 times if you want to complete each encounter rather than run past enemies,

This was my frist time playing a JRPG so I don't know if this is normal in this genre, but endgame is very grindy. So much so, that I didn't even bother to do some endgame content, because I'd need to farm mobs for hours before I could possibly have a shot at the bosses.

100% worth it to play for the story alone. It's up there with the likes of The Last of Us, God of War and Red Dead Redemption 2, and the combat is fun too.

In a world of ADHD fast paced games, it's nice to see a game breathe. The score is memorable, the cut scenes are realtime. This is a game I would play again--the first time for the story, the second for the side quests.

Clair Obscur is a great game, but it's definitely not a perfect one. The exploration feels very dated; There are invisible walls everywhere, and locations that seem like they're supposed to be revisited offer very little reason to actually come back. I had to look up guides at least twice because I just couldn't find my way to the next area. Outside of the combat - which is excellent - the whole game feels a bit dated. With that said, Clair Obscur sets out to do something specific, and it nails it.

It's absolutely not perfect, but it's easy excuse the flaws the game has because of how well it executes its core ideas. It's one of the best games I've played, and I would highly recommend it to anyone.
